title: Stripe webhook handler does not verify the signature header

applicability.reason: Project ships a live Stripe webhook route that grants entitlements.

evidence.description: Handler parses request.json() directly; stripe.webhooks.constructEvent is never called.

evidence: No STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is referenced anywhere in the repository.

behavioral_evidence.description: POST with a forged body and no stripe-signature header returned 200 and wrote an entitlement row.

research_summary: Signature verification is the documented requirement for trusting webhook payloads; unverified handlers accept forged events.

codex_review.summary: Independent review reached the same conclusion and added a replay-attack path.

risk: Anyone who can reach the endpoint can grant themselves paid entitlements.
recommended_remediation: Verify the stripe-signature header with stripe.webhooks.constructEvent before any processing.
Add an idempotency key on the Stripe event id.
verification_steps: Replay a forged request and confirm a 400 response.
Replay a genuine event twice and confirm one entitlement row.

title: CCPA business-threshold applicability cannot be determined from the repository

applicability.reason: Applicability turns on business facts that do not exist in the codebase.
facts_required: Annual gross revenue for the prior calendar year
Number of California consumers whose personal information was processed
Whether personal information is sold or shared for cross-context behavioral advertising

evidence: Repository contains no revenue, customer-count, or data-sale records.
research_summary: California access by users alone does not establish applicability; thresholds must be checked against current statutory text.

codex_review.unavailable_reason: not required for an UNKNOWN applicability record

risk: Unresolved applicability leaves the disclosure obligations unassessed.
recommended_remediation: Provide the listed business facts so applicability can be assessed.

title: Public bucket contains only marketing logos

applicability.reason: Project uses object storage with one public bucket.

evidence.description: Bucket 'public-assets' is public and contains only brand logo files.

behavioral_evidence.description: Anonymous listing of the private 'user-uploads' bucket returned 403.

research_summary: A public bucket is not by itself a vulnerability; only the contents decide.

codex_review.summary: Independent review confirmed no user data in the public bucket.

verification_steps: Re-list both buckets anonymously after any storage change.

adversarial_challenge.summary: Challenged as a critical-control PASS; anonymous access to private objects stayed denied.
